title: HubSpot timeline event + task naming/copy conventions for PLG signals
creator: Chris Osei
description:
## Context
We’re piping PLG “sales-worthy” signals (usage thresholds + intent events) into HubSpot as Company timeline events, and using workflows to auto-create tasks and enroll sequences. During pilot prep, Sales + Biz Systems flagged that the current event names are inconsistent and hard to scan (varied capitalization, unclear signal type, too much text in the name, no clear “what to do next”).

This ticket defines the naming + copy structure for:
- HubSpot **Company timeline events** created by the signal routing service
- HubSpot **tasks** created by workflows (SDR/AEs) based on the signal event

Goal: an AE should be able to glance at the timeline and understand:
1) what happened (signal type)
2) why it matters (one line, with key metric)
3) what action to take (CTA)
4) where to click (links to Console / dashboard / runbook)

Non-goals:
- Re-defining signal thresholds/scoring
- HubSpot workflow logic or ownership rules (covered in PM-413)
- Slack notification format (covered in DES-231)

## Principles
- **Scanability first:** event NAME must be short, consistent, and sortable.
- **Put details in the body:** name indicates the category; body contains metrics + context.
- **Avoid jargon:** prefer “Rate limit hits” over “429s” in the event name; include the HTTP code in body.
- **No user-level identifiers:** company-level only (aligned with security guidance).
- **Stable naming:** don’t encode thresholds in the event name (thresholds change); include the observed value(s) + window in body.

## Timeline event conventions
### 1) Timeline event Name (what AEs see in the left rail)
Use this fixed pattern:

**PLG Signal — {Signal Type}**

- Prefix always: **“PLG Signal —”** (enables quick filtering/search)
- Signal Type: Title Case, short noun phrase
- No emojis, no exclamation, no dates, no thresholds

Approved Signal Type values (v1):
- **Spend Growth**
- **Rate Limit Friction**
- **Concurrency Spike**
- **Reliability Errors**
- **Model Routing Failures**
- **Dedicated Interest**
- **Private / VPC Interest**
- **Security Intent**
- **Region / Residency Need**
- **Contact Sales**

Notes:
- Prefer “Private / VPC Interest” over “Private Deployment Interest” to keep length down.
- Use “Region / Residency Need” to cover both residency flags and explicit region selection constraints.
- If HubSpot UI truncates long names, the prefix + type should still read well.

### 2) Timeline event Body (details)
Body should follow the same structure across signals, with 3–6 lines max before links. Use labels (bold) for scanability.

**Recommended body template (plaintext):**

**Summary:** {one sentence human summary}
**Observed:** {metric(s) + window(s)}
**Why it matters:** {1 sentence tie to Dedicated/Private/security value}
**Recommended next step:** {single action}
**Links:** Console • Usage dashboard • Pricing/packaging guidance
**Routing:** Owner={AE/SDR} • Segment={segment} • Cooldown={X days} • Dedupe={key}

Body requirements:
- Always include **at least one observed metric** and the aggregation window (7/14/30d).
- Always include a **recommended next step** (examples below).
- Links must be full URLs (HubSpot strips relative links in some views).
- “Routing” line is for internal auditability; keep it as the last line.

### 3) Signal-specific copy blocks (examples)
Below are examples to standardize tone and the “recommended next step” language.

A) PLG Signal — Spend Growth
**Summary:** Self-serve usage is growing quickly and may be nearing Hosted plan limits.
**Observed:** Spend: $3,420 (30d) ↑ 62% vs prior 30d • Tokens: 190M (30d)
**Why it matters:** Dedicated capacity can stabilize latency/throughput and unlock commit-based pricing.
**Recommended next step:** Offer a 15-min performance/capacity review and discuss Dedicated sizing.
**Links:** {Console usage} • {Cost breakdown} • {Packaging guidance}
**Routing:** Owner=…

B) PLG Signal — Rate Limit Friction
**Summary:** Repeated rate limiting suggests the workload is bursting above current quota.
**Observed:** 429s: 14 days with >50/day • Peak RPS: 180 • Top route: /v1/chat.completions
**Why it matters:** Dedicated pools reduce throttling risk and provide predictable throughput.
**Recommended next step:** Ask about concurrency targets and propose Dedicated PoC.

C) PLG Signal — Security Intent
**Summary:** High intent around enterprise security controls.
**Observed:** Viewed: SSO/SAML docs (3x) • Audit logs docs (2x) • Security questionnaire started
**Why it matters:** Private/VPC + enterprise controls shorten procurement and unblock production rollouts.
**Recommended next step:** Offer a security readiness call; share SOC 2 + SSO + audit log overview.

D) PLG Signal — Region / Residency Need
**Summary:** Region choice/residency needs may require Dedicated/Private deployment.
**Observed:** Region selected: eu-west • Residency flag: EU-only • Requests served outside region: 8% (7d)
**Why it matters:** Dedicated in-region or Private VPC improves residency posture and reduces risk.
**Recommended next step:** Confirm residency requirements and map to Dedicated region options.

## Task conventions (created by HubSpot workflows)
HubSpot tasks should read like a “next action” checklist item, not a system log.

### 1) Task Title
Use verb-first, concise pattern:

**Follow up on PLG signal: {Signal Type}**

Examples:
- Follow up on PLG signal: Rate Limit Friction
- Follow up on PLG signal: Security Intent

### 2) Task Notes (task body)
First line should repeat the “recommended next step” in plain language, then include a short pasteable snippet.

Template:
- **Next step:** {recommended next step sentence}
- **Use this opener:** “Noticed you’ve been hitting rate limits during spikes—open to a quick review of throughput targets and options like Dedicated capacity?”
- **What to check:** {1–3 bullets}
- **Links:** HubSpot record • Console • Playbook

### 3) Ownership + SLA copy
To reduce confusion during pilot, include a single line in the task notes:

**SLA:** First touch within 1 business day (pilot)

(Workflow logic will handle escalations; this is only copy to set expectations.)

## Guardrails / do-not-do
- Do not include personal names, email addresses, IPs, or message contents from support tickets.
- Do not include pricing/discount promises in event bodies (keep it to “discuss commit-based pricing” and link to internal guidance).
- Do not include “P0/P1” or internal severity codes in the name; if needed, use “Why it matters” sentence.

## Implementation notes for Eng + Biz Systems
- Event name is a function of the **signal_type enum** only.
- Event body can embed dynamic fields. Keep to a consistent order.
- If fields are missing (e.g., no tokens for embeddings-only accounts), omit the line rather than inserting “N/A”.
- Truncation: keep body under ~1,500 characters to avoid UI clipping in some HubSpot views.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Standardized event name format with approved signal type strings
- [x] Standardized body template and 4+ signal examples
- [x] Standardized task title + notes templates
- [x] Reviewed by Sales Ops + Biz Systems + SDR lead for readability

## Links / references
- Confluence PRD: PLG→Sales signal routing (requirements)
- PM-413: HubSpot routing requirements
- DES-231: Slack notification format
- Drive: SDR sequence drafts (for opener alignment)

## Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should we include the score in the name? A: No. Include score in body only (Routing line), if needed for debugging.
- Q: Should we include “Expansion” vs “New logo” in the name? A: No (routing can differ, but name stays stable). If useful, include “Segment” in Routing line.
